summary: Low overall risk. Solid security fundamentals with only two minor issues (one medium, one low) and comprehensive protective measures.

vulnerabilities.description: Garmin login failure messages include full exception details that are sent via Telegram. While restricted to authenticated users with configured Telegram tokens, this could leak implementation details in error scenarios.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize Telegram messages to user-friendly text while keeping full details in server logs. Example: 'Garmin login failed. Check credentials and network connectivity. Full error logged.'

vulnerabilities.description: Hint text states 'Stored locally, never committed' but tokens are actually in sessionStorage (volatile), not localStorage. Clarification needed that sessionStorage is cleared when browser session ends.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update hint text to: 'Stored in browser session only — cleared when you close the browser or tab.'

strengths: Path traversal protection: Both /contents/ and /static routes use is_relative_to() to prevent directory escape
DoS mitigation on auth: MAX_BODY (1 MiB) cap prevents unauthenticated login endpoint from unbounded memory allocation
Constant-time auth: Uses hmac.compare_digest() for both username and password to prevent timing attacks
Secure session cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Lax flags set correctly
XML safety: Hand-rolled parser only handles standard entities; no XXE or entity expansion risk
Token hygiene: Garmin credentials never logged; Strava/intervals.icu keys in volatile sessionStorage (cleared on browser close)
Input validation: Numeric ranges enforced (RPE 1-10, power 0-2000, cadence bounds, etc.)
Rate limiting: Global lock adds 1-second delay on failed login attempts
No hardcoded secrets: All sensitive config via environment variables (.env.example guide only)
No SQL injection surface: File-based JSON store, no database queries
No CSRF: Authenticated endpoints require session cookies
No XSS: Uses textContent, not innerHTML for user input; HTML escaping in place

verification_checklist.sql_injection: PASS - No SQL queries; JSON-based file storage only
verification_checklist.xxe_entity_expansion: PASS - Custom XML parser safe; only standard entities decoded
verification_checklist.csrf: PASS - Endpoints require session authentication; no cross-origin forms
verification_checklist.hardcoded_credentials: PASS - All secrets in environment; .env.example is template only
verification_checklist.password_handling: PASS - Never logged; scrypt hashing with constant-time comparison
verification_checklist.xss: PASS - textContent used for untrusted data; escapeHtml() helper in place
verification_checklist.path_traversal: PASS - is_relative_to() checks prevent directory escape
verification_checklist.dos_mitigation: PASS - HTTP body limit (1 MiB), socket timeout (30s), per-IP rate limiting
verification_checklist.authentication: PASS - Scrypt-based, constant-time comparison, secure cookie flags
verification_checklist.authorization: PASS - Session-based; internal port bypasses auth by design (trusted loopback only)

recommendations: Priority 1: Sanitize Garmin error messages in Telegram notifications to user-friendly text
Priority 2: Clarify sessionStorage token lifetime in UI hints
Optional: Consider OAuth2 token refresh for Strava/intervals.icu to reduce manual token management
Optional: Add log rotation (current: unbounded growth of sync logs; suggest keep latest 500 runs)

protections: Credentials routed through WARP; never logged or persisted
Volatile storage; cleared on browser close
Volatile storage; cleared on browser close

conclusion: PaceForge maintains a strong security posture for a single-athlete fitness coaching app. The two identified issues are minor (one informational, one UI clarity) and do not represent security breaches. All critical attack surfaces are protected against SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, and DoS. No hardcoded secrets in source. Recommended fixes are enhancements to already-safe behavior.
